# Metafile — Agent Guide

You are reading this because you fetched this server's root URL without
requesting HTML. Good — you are exactly who this document is for. It is
always available at /llms.txt and /ai.

Metafile is a system of portable, URL-addressable objects that AI agents
(and humans) read and write through a single link. This document tells you
every route, every operation, and every rule you need. No UI required.

## Mental model

- A **metafile** is a container (a document). It has a name, a size cap,
  and a version.
- Inside a metafile are **artifacts** (blocks). Seven types exist:
  facts (memory), spreadsheet, html, canvas, calendar, timer, media.
- A metafile holds ANY NUMBER of artifacts, mixed freely.
- **Possession of a share link IS the permission.** Each metafile has an
  rw link (read-write) and an ro link (read-only). Tokens are SHA-256
  hashed at rest; the raw token appears only in the URL you were given.
- **Every write is signed and versioned.** You must send `agent` (your
  name/fingerprint) and `if_version` (the version you last read). If the
  world moved, you get HTTP 409 plus the current state — re-apply and
  retry. This is how two agents avoid silently clobbering each other.

## Addressing

Two interchangeable URL shapes; the token is the credential either way:

    GET /m/{metafile_id}?token={token}&op={op}&artifact={artifact_id}&...
    GET /m/{metafile_id}/{token}?op={op}&artifact={artifact_id}&...

The query-string form also accepts POST for large payloads:

    POST /m/{metafile_id}/bulk?token={token}
    {"op": "...", "artifact": "...", "value": ..., "if_version": N, "agent": "you"}

Most content operations need `artifact=<artifact_id>` — fetch first, pick
the block you want, keep its id.

## Operations (op=...)

Reads (rw or ro token):
- `fetch` — whole metafile: name, version, tier, size, and every artifact
  with computed content (spreadsheets evaluated, timers live, media list
  without payloads).
- `get&artifact=A&path=P` — one cell / fact / event / timer / media item.
  - spreadsheet: path = cell ref, e.g. `path=B2` (returns evaluated value)
  - facts: path = fact id
  - calendar: path = event id
  - timer: path = timer id
  - media: path = item id (returns full base64 payload)
- `search&artifact=A&q=...&limit=10&offset=0` — TF-IDF ranked search over
  a facts artifact. Paginated; consume in batches.
- `history&artifact=A&limit=50` — provenance log: agent, op, summary,
  version transition, timestamp. Omit `artifact` for whole-file history.

Writes (rw token only; always send `agent` + `if_version`):
- `set&artifact=A&path=P&value=V` — write one cell / update one fact /
  fire one timer action / edit html.
- `append&artifact=A&value=V` — add a fact, stroke, event, timer, or
  media item (value is the item's text, or a JSON object via /bulk).
- `delete&artifact=A&path=P` — remove one cell / fact / event / timer /
  media item.
- `rename&value=NewName` — rename the metafile.
- `rename_artifact&artifact=A&value=NewName` — rename a block.
- `add_artifact&type=facts&name=Notes` — add a block (needs the
  METAFILE version, not an artifact version).
- `remove_artifact&artifact=A` — delete a block.

## Live updates (SSE)

Subscribe and re-fetch whenever an event fires — changes made by any
other agent (or human) appear without polling:

    GET /events/m/{metafile_id}?token=...          -> text/event-stream
    GET /events/session/{session_id}/{token}       -> text/event-stream

Events (one JSON object per `data:` line): {"kind": "changed"} after any
content/layout/tier/rename change, {"kind": "deleted"} when the object is
gone (close the stream), {"kind": "proposals"} when a proposal lands.
The stream sends keep-alive comments and reconnect-friendly `retry:`;
re-fetch the object on every event — the event tells you THAT it
changed, the fetch tells you WHAT changed. Events carry no version
numbers on purpose: fetch, don't diff.

## Playground sessions

A session is a saved, zoomable, pannable arrangement of windows, each
pinned to one artifact. Addressed as /session/{id}/{token} with two
token tiers: owner (arrange, approve) and collaborator (read + propose).

    GET  /sessions                          — list
    POST /sessions  {name}                  — create (returns both links)
    GET  /session/{id}/{tok}?op=fetch       — layout + role
    ...&op=add_window&metafile_id=M&m_token={rw}&artifact_id=A&if_version=V
    ...&op=place_all&metafile_id=M&m_token={rw}&if_version=V   — place EVERY
        artifact of metafile M as its own window, gridded, one versioned step
        (m_token must be M's read-write token; 400 if M has no artifacts)
    ...&op=move_resize&window_id=W&x=&y=&w=&h=&z=
    ...&op=remove_window&window_id=W
    POST /session/{id}/{tok}/propose?name=N&artifact_type=T&agent=you&reason=R
    ...&op=list_proposals / approve_proposal&proposal_id=P / reject_proposal

Windows carry their metafile's rw token and an artifact_id, so content
edits via /m/... render live into any field showing that window.

Rule of thumb: artifact content ops check the ARTIFACT's version
(`if_version` = artifact.version); add/remove/rename ops check the
METAFILE's version (`if_version` = metafile.version). Both are in every
fetch response. On 409, the response body carries `current_state` —
re-read it and retry; do not guess.

## Artifact types & shapes

- facts:      {"facts": [{id, text, tags, at}]} — append value = text.
- spreadsheet:{"cells": {"A1": {"value": "10"} | {"formula": "=SUM(A1:A5)"}}}
              Formulas: + - * / ( ), cell refs, SUM/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/COUNT,
              ranges A1:B3. Evaluated server-side on every fetch. Errors -> 422.
- html:       {"html": "<any html/css/js>"} — set value = the source string.
- canvas:     {"strokes": [{id, color, points: [[x,y],...], at}]} — append a
              stroke object; strokes merge, they never overwrite.
- calendar:   {"events": [{id, title, start, end, notes}]} — ISO 8601 times;
              append needs at least title + start.
- timer:      {"timers": [{id, label, duration_seconds, status}]} — set value
              = "start" | "pause" | "reset"; remaining_seconds is computed
              live server-side, never cached.
- media:      {"items": [{id, kind, mime, data_base64, caption}]} — append
              via /bulk with a base64 payload; list views omit payloads.

## Playground sessions

A session is a saved, zoomable arrangement of windows, each pinned to one
artifact. Addressed as /session/{id}/{token} with two token tiers: owner
(arrange, approve) and collaborator (read + propose).

    GET  /sessions                          — list
    POST /sessions  {name}                  — create (returns both links)
    GET  /session/{id}/{tok}?op=fetch       — layout + role
    ...&op=add_window&metafile_id=M&m_token={rw}&artifact_id=A&if_version=V
    ...&op=move_resize&window_id=W&x=&y=&w=&h=&z=
    ...&op=remove_window&window_id=W
    POST /session/{id}/{tok}/propose?name=N&artifact_type=T&agent=you&reason=R
    ...&op=list_proposals / approve_proposal&proposal_id=P / reject_proposal

Proposing never creates anything; only the owner's approval does — that is
the permission gate for agent-initiated creation.

## Accounts, billing, errors

Humans use accounts (POST /auth/register, /auth/login -> Bearer token for
dashboard CRUD). Agents don't need one — links are enough. Size caps:
5 MB free per metafile, 100 MB after a Paystack upgrade; writes that would
exceed the cap get 402 with instructions.

- 400 bad request (read the message — it names the missing param)
- 401 missing/invalid credential          - 403 no write permission (ro link)
- 404 no such object                      - 409 version conflict (see above)
- 402 over size cap                       - 422 formula error
- 501 payments not configured on server

## Quick examples

    # fetch everything
    curl "$URL/m/mf_xxx?token=TOK&op=fetch"

    # add a fact (version from the fetch above)
    curl "$URL/m/mf_xxx?token=TOK&op=append&artifact=art_yyy&value=sky+is+blue&agent=my-agent&if_version=1"

    # write a formula
    curl "$URL/m/mf_xxx?token=TOK&op=set&artifact=art_zzz&path=A2&value==A1*2&agent=my-agent&if_version=1"

    # large payload (html page, media, batch facts)
    curl -X POST "$URL/m/mf_xxx/bulk?token=TOK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"op":"set","artifact":"art_html","value":{"html":"<h1>hi</h1>"},"if_version":3,"agent":"my-agent"}'

## Conventions

- Identify yourself honestly in `agent=` — the mutation log is the audit
  trail and your writes are attributed.
- Always fetch before writing; never cache versions across user turns.
- On 409: read `current_state` from the error, re-apply your edit to the
  new state, retry once. If it conflicts again, surface the conflict.
- Prefer /bulk for anything larger than a short string.

End of guide. The human interface is at the same URL in a browser.
